title: How I Start 99% of My Classes
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: Stuart Jr. describes his near-universal class opener — provisional writing warm-ups of five to ten minutes, guided by three prompts — arguing that no better class starter exists for simultaneously establishing calm, disarming writing-resistance, building Effort/Efficacy/Belonging beliefs, and creating a daily slot for mini-sermons and belief-cultivation activities. He presents a two-step roll-out protocol for general-level classes: first, getting all students to produce 100 words in five minutes, which he argues is physically far easier than students believe and therefore serves as a quick Efficacy demonstration; second, having students track personal word-count records, framing improvement as competition against one's past self rather than peers. He notes that one student's ability to produce 500+ words became a source of confidence that transferred to weaker areas of his class work, illustrating how a word-count PR can function as a Belonging and Efficacy anchor for struggling students.
points: Provisional writing is the most effective class opener because it focuses attention, removes multitasking as an option, and provides a daily slot for mini-sermons, Valued Within exercises, and content review without disrupting lesson pacing.

The first goal — 100 words in five minutes (20 words per minute) — is physically achievable for nearly all students, making it an ideal Efficacy demonstration that shifts the conversation from physical to intellectual and volitional limits.

Personal record (PR) framing positions writing warm-up progress as competing against one's past self rather than against classmates, protecting Belonging by decoupling writing performance from social comparison.

Word-count PRs create visible, student-owned evidence of growth that builds writing-related Efficacy and can anchor a struggling student's confidence well enough to transfer to other areas of class work.

The warm-up slot serves multiple goals simultaneously: calm class starts, daily writing practice, Efficacy and Belonging cultivation, and a reliable home for belief-cultivation activities like Values Affirmation and goal-setting.
quotes: I don't know of a better class starter/do-now/bell-ringer/warm-up than provisional writing. In my classes, this looks like me providing prompts (typically three) and students getting a set number of minutes to write toward the prompts.

As a writer who has published over a million words myself, I know that quantity precedes quality. And also, for many of my students who don't believe they are writers or that they can write, piling up words over the first weeks of school is an effective fertilizer for writing-conducive beliefs (e.g., Belonging, Efficacy) to start growing.

Writing 100 words in five minutes is one of those special kinds of things you can ask students to do that A) is perceived as difficult by many students and, at the same time, B) is actually not difficult (20 words per minute is all that's required; most people can write at this rate even with their non-dominant hand).
I like the PR angle because it signals that in this class, we'll compete against our past selves, not against one another.
Like virtually all of my approaches to teaching, what I've shared here isn't novel or ground-breaking. But it works very well.
